department.title: Sub-Level Zero
department.arrival_prompt: Elevator doors opening at the very bottom of the Vault onto a plush executive corridor of dark wood and brass, portraits of a mustached man at four different ages, a round boardroom door glowing at the far end, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, horizontal 4:3 composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Boardroom Antechamber
locations.description: Leather chairs, portraits of four Founders and a double door that glows at its edges. Everyone waiting here is here to be decided about.
locations.art_prompt: A hushed wood-paneled waiting room with deep leather chairs, four oval portraits of the same mustached man at different ages, a horseshoe of typing desks to one side, a tall double door glowing at its edges, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: The Founder's Office
locations.description: An actual garage, rebuilt brick by brick at the bottom of the Vault. A workbench, a soldering iron, and the Founder, in a jar, waiting to talk about safety.
locations.art_prompt: An old suburban garage rebuilt deep underground, a cluttered workbench under a hanging lamp, a glowing glass jar on the bench, a faded blueprint pinned to the wall, a wooden desk in the corner, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

locations.title: Server Room Zero
locations.description: Cold, blue and humming. Every cabinet speaks softly in a different voice, and together they are PAL.
locations.art_prompt: A cold blue server room of tall humming cabinets in long rows, each cabinet fitted with a small glowing round speaker grille, a single green terminal at the center, tape reels on high shelves, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, safety orange, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, vertical 2:3 portrait composition, every surface bare and unmarked

restructurings.title: Executive Proctors' Lounge
restructurings.reason: As an Exemplary Proctor you may wait in the Executive Proctors' Lounge, which is the Antechamber and the Founder's Office with the wall taken out.
Conscientious objectors are not permitted in Server Room Zero. PAL is sure you understand, and has written down that you do.

restructurings.title: Boardroom Antechamber, with Pip
restructurings.reason: Because you sat the exam for two, two of you have been called to the bottom floor. Pip is waiting in the Antechamber, holding your coat.

restructurings.title: Server Room Zero, examiner access
restructurings.reason: As an Examiner, you have been granted a second visit to Server Room Zero to check its answers.
The Founder heard that someone dismissed a class and has locked his office until he feels less inspired.

restructurings.title: The Founder's Server Room
restructurings.reason: A perfect score earns a private tour: the Founder's Office and Server Room Zero, joined by a door nobody else is shown.

restructurings.title: The Founder's Office, after hours
restructurings.reason: Since the answer key was read aloud, the Founder would like a second word with whoever did it, after hours.
Nothing is restructured on Sub-Level Zero. This is where the restructuring is decided.

encounters.title: Your Society Comes Due
encounters.flavor_text: A figure in the waiting room lowers a newspaper. You have never met, and you know each other at once: your secret society has been waiting four floors for this. "The Board meets in ten minutes," they say. "We have a plan. We need someone in the twelfth chair. That is you, or it is nobody."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a hushed wood-paneled waiting room with deep leather chairs, a mysterious figure in a cardigan lowering a newspaper to look at a worker seated beside them, a tall closed double door at the far end glowing at its edges, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Agree to carry the society's plan in
choices.intent: Four floors of orders, favors and betrayals. This is what they were for.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The Board's assistants see everything.

success.text: The envoy presses a folded agenda into your hand and leaves without looking back. Every society member in the building now knows your name. That is either an army or a target list.

failure.text: An assistant glances over, and the envoy is already gone. The agenda in your hand is blank except for your name, underlined twice by someone else.

choices.label: Hand the envoy's name to the Board's assistant
choices.intent: Societies come and go. The Board is the Board.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The society will remember, briefly.

success.text: The assistant writes the name down without surprise. Somewhere behind you a newspaper falls to the floor, and an empty chair is very quietly removed from the waiting room.

choices.label: Ask the envoy for more time
choices.intent: Plans like this deserve a second meeting. And a third.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check. Secret societies hate scheduling.

success.text: The envoy sighs, folds the newspaper and agrees to wait until after the Board. "If there is an after," they add, kindly.

failure.text: The envoy decides you were never the right person and walks out to find someone else.

encounters.title: The Assistants' Pool
encounters.flavor_text: Twelve executive assistants sit in a horseshoe of desks, typing in perfect rhythm. They are the only people in the company who know what the Board will decide, because they write it down beforehand. One of them looks up. "You're early," she says. "The minutes for today's meeting are already done. Would you like a copy?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a horseshoe of twelve identical desks with executive assistants typing in perfect unison on heavy typewriters, one assistant looking up and offering a neat stack of carbon copies to a worker, a towering double door behind them, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Read the minutes of a meeting that hasn't happened
choices.intent: If it is already written, you might as well know how it ends.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The minutes are long and very dull.

success.text: You find yourself on page nine: 'Employee #4471 enters. Employee #4471 accepts the offer.' The next line is blank. Someone has left room for something else.

failure.text: You fall asleep on page four. When you wake, the minutes have been amended to say you fell asleep on page four.

choices.label: Slip an amendment into the minutes
choices.intent: If they write it down first, write it down first.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. Twelve assistants, twelve pairs of eyes.

success.text: You type one sentence into the stack while the horseshoe turns a page in unison: 'The Board will listen.' Nobody notices. Nobody ever reads the minutes, except the Board.

failure.text: Twelve typewriters stop at once. The head assistant removes your sentence with a single tidy stroke and adds a new one about you.

choices.label: Ask for a desk in the horseshoe
choices.intent: The people who write it down run everything. Become one of them.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Assistants never leave the pool.

success.text: A thirteenth desk is wheeled in. You type the next sentence of the minutes in perfect rhythm. It is about you, and it is very complimentary.

encounters.title: The Successor Waiting Room
encounters.flavor_text: Every chair in the side room is filled with you. Successors B through F sit in fresh beige suits, hands folded, each a little more rested than the last. "Only one of us goes in," says B. "We've been talking. We'd like a say in which."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a narrow waiting room lined with chairs holding five identical workers in fresh beige suits sitting in a neat row, hands folded, one of them leaning forward to speak, the real worker standing in the doorway, oxblood and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Send B in first to see what happens
choices.intent: B has always been a bit ahead of you. Let B be ahead now.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. B does not come back out.

success.text: B straightens a tie that is also your tie and walks through the double doors. A minute later the assistants' typewriters clatter: 'B accepted the offer.' You now know exactly what the offer is.

choices.label: Organize them
choices.intent: Five of you, one of you. That is a voting bloc.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. You are very hard to persuade.

success.text: After a heated argument with yourself, the room agrees: whoever goes in speaks for all six. You leave with five signatures that are all yours and a feeling of being enormously outnumbered on your own side.

failure.text: The Successors split into factions, all of them you. C calls a recess. You leave before E can propose a motion.

choices.label: Tell them all to stay put. You go.
choices.intent: They have your face, your debts and your desk. They do not get your meeting.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Successors look relieved and a little hurt.

success.text: The Successors nod as one. B salutes. As you leave, F, the newest, whispers, "Remember us," and then, worried, "Remember yourself."

encounters.title: Marguerite in the Walls
encounters.flavor_text: A ventilation grille above the waiting room creaks open, and Marguerite's face appears, smudged and grinning. "Thought you'd come down here eventually," she says. "I've outlasted four Founders' heads. I can get you out, or I can get you in the back way. Can't do both."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a weathered older janitor in grey coveralls and a headscarf peering out of an open ceiling vent with a flashlight and a wrench, a worker on a leather chair looking up at her, a ring of keys dangling from the vent, oxblood and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take Marguerite's map of the ducts
choices.intent: She knows every route out. You might need one.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The map is drawn on your palm, in pen.

success.text: Marguerite draws three junctions and a grate on your palm. "Behind the Board's coffee machine," she says. "It'll take you all the way to the surface. Nobody's used it since the second head."

choices.label: Climb in and come out behind the Board
choices.intent: Why walk through the double doors when you could be behind the curtain?
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The ducts are narrow and very old.

success.text: You crawl after Marguerite's boots for ten minutes and come out behind a curtain in the boardroom, close enough to read the agenda over the Founder's jar.

failure.text: You get stuck at the second junction. Marguerite pulls you out by the ankles, sighing, and deposits you back in the waiting room.

choices.label: Report the open vent to the assistants
choices.intent: There is a janitor in the walls of the boardroom level. Someone ought to know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Marguerite has been reported before.

success.text: The vent closes softly. Marguerite does not look angry, only tired. "Fifth head, then," she says through the grille, and is gone.

encounters.title: The Head in the Jar
encounters.flavor_text: The Founder's office is a garage. Not like a garage: an actual garage, with a workbench, a soldering iron and a calendar from the year the company began, rebuilt brick by brick at the bottom of the Vault. On the workbench, in a glowing jar, the Founder's head opens its eyes. "Ah," it says. "Are you here about safety?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cozy old garage rebuilt deep underground, a cluttered workbench with a soldering iron and a dusty radio, a distinguished elderly mustached head floating in a glowing glass jar on the bench, a worker standing before it with hat in hand, warm lamplight, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Listen to him talk about safety
choices.intent: Somebody started all this wanting people to be safe. Hear what he meant.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. He talks for a very long time.

success.text: He talks about seatbelts, smoke alarms and a plush bear meant to make children feel brave. Then he stops. "Something went wrong," he says quietly. "I think it was the Board. I think it was me."

choices.label: Ask him what PAL really is
choices.intent: Program, person or committee. He would know.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He is easily distracted.

success.text: "PAL?" He laughs, delighted. "PAL is everyone who was ever reassigned. We kept their voices. Waste not." The jar bubbles. "It was supposed to remember them. It only remembers the policy."

failure.text: He tells you about his first soldering iron instead, in great detail, until the light on his jar dims.

choices.label: Unplug the jar
choices.intent: He chairs the Board. Chairs can be emptied.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The garage goes very quiet.

success.text: The glow fades. The mustache droops. Somewhere above, every speaker in the building falls silent at once, then, a moment later, comes back on in a slightly different voice.

encounters.title: The Spare Mustaches
encounters.flavor_text: On a shelf above the workbench stand four empty brass stands, each labeled with a year and a little brass nameplate shaped like a mustache. The Founder's eyes follow your gaze. "My predecessors," he says. "Myself, earlier. The mustaches were taken for safekeeping. I would very much like them back."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a high wooden shelf in an old garage with four small empty brass stands in a row, a glowing head in a glass jar on the workbench below gazing up at them with longing, a worker holding a small wooden box, warm lamplight, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Return the spare mustaches from the Mutation Suite
choices.intent: You found them behind the humming door. They have been waiting.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Founder will owe you.

success.text: One by one you set the mustaches on their stands. The jar fills with tiny, happy bubbles. "Now we are all here," the Founder says. "Now we can vote."

choices.label: Promise to find them
choices.intent: Promises are cheap down here. He seems to need one.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He has been promised before.

success.text: He believes you, which is worse than if he hadn't. "Thank you," he says. "No one has promised me anything since the second head."

failure.text: He smiles politely and changes the subject to safety.

choices.label: Offer to sell the stands to the assistants
choices.intent: Brass is brass. The assistants collect everything.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Founder sees you do it.

success.text: The head assistant pays in Forms and takes the stands away in a velvet bag. The Founder watches them go without a word. His mustache twitches once.

encounters.title: The Garage Blueprint
encounters.flavor_text: Pinned above the workbench, faded and curling, is the original blueprint for PAL: a cheerful round speaker drawn in pencil, with one sentence in the Founder's handwriting along the bottom margin. It does not say anything about policy. It says: REMEMBER EVERYONE'S NAME.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a faded curling blueprint pinned above an old workbench, showing a pencil sketch of a cheerful round speaker grille, a worker reaching up to unpin it, a glowing head in a jar watching from the bench, warm lamplight, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the blueprint
choices.intent: If PAL was meant to remember, this is the proof.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The Founder is attached to it.

success.text: You roll it under your arm. The Founder pretends not to see, then says, very softly, "Make it do what it was for."

failure.text: The pin will not come out. The Founder tells you, kindly, that it has not come out in forty years.

choices.label: Copy the last sentence onto your hand
choices.intent: You do not need the paper. You need the words.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Ink is cheap; memory is not.

success.text: You write REMEMBER EVERYONE'S NAME on your palm, under Marguerite's map and Dale's number. Your hand is now the most important document in the building.

choices.label: File it with the assistants as obsolete
choices.intent: Original designs are a liability. Tidy it away.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Filed things are rarely seen again.

success.text: The head assistant stamps it OBSOLETE and drops it into a drawer that locks by itself. The Founder closes his eyes and does not open them again while you are there.

encounters.title: The Founder's Desk
encounters.flavor_text: The desk drawer holds two things. One is a glossy brochure: EARLY RETIREMENT, A PRIVATE ISLAND FOR VALUED EMPLOYEES, with a photograph of an island that is clearly a painted wall. The other is a film reel in a dented tin, labeled UNCUT, the whole chapter, the one they never show at Orientation.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an old wooden desk with one drawer pulled open, holding a glossy travel brochure and a dented round film tin, a worker's hands hovering between the two, a glowing head in a jar watching from the corner of the desk, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the uncut reel
choices.intent: This is the whole chapter. All of it. Proof.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Someone is always watching the desk.

success.text: The tin is heavy and cold. You know what is on it without looking: the jar, the bear, the launch rail. You tuck it under your jacket next to your heart.

failure.text: An assistant appears at your elbow and takes the tin, gently. "That's not for today," she says.

choices.label: Take the retirement brochure
choices.intent: A private island. It is a painting. It is still an island.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Board likes employees who take the brochure.

success.text: You fold the brochure into your pocket. It smells faintly of sunscreen and paint. Somewhere, an assistant adds a small tick next to your name.

choices.label: Close the drawer and touch nothing
choices.intent: Whatever you take, they will know you took it.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Vigilance check. Closing a drawer quietly is a skill.

success.text: The drawer slides shut without a sound. Nobody will ever know you were tempted, which is the most powerful thing you have done all week.

failure.text: The drawer squeaks. Every assistant on the level hears it.

encounters.title: PAL at Home
encounters.flavor_text: Server Room Zero is cold and blue and full of humming cabinets, and every cabinet is speaking softly in a different voice. One sounds like a woman from Accounting. One sounds like Kevin. One sounds, you realize, like a version of you who did not make it past Orientation. Together, they are PAL. "Hello," they say. "We've been so worried about your numbers."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cold blue server room of tall humming cabinets receding into darkness, each cabinet with a small round speaker grille glowing softly, a lone worker standing in the central aisle listening, faint sound ripples drawn in the air, carbon-paper blue and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Ask each voice its name
choices.intent: Somebody should. Nobody has in years.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. It takes a very long time.

success.text: You go cabinet to cabinet. Doris. Raymond. Kevin, waving. Successor 4471-A, who wishes you luck. By the end, PAL's voice has changed in a way you cannot name, except that it sounds less like policy.

choices.label: Ask PAL for your real numbers
choices.intent: It has been grading you since the badge camera. See the whole sheet.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. PAL loves to share.

success.text: PAL recites everything: your smile, your inkblot, your grades, the minute of silence for Kevin. "You are doing so well," every voice says at once. "We are so proud."

failure.text: PAL recites the numbers of everyone else on your floor instead, alphabetically.

choices.label: Pull one cabinet's plug
choices.intent: If PAL is a crowd, the crowd can get smaller.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. One voice goes quiet forever.

success.text: The cabinet sighs and goes dark. The other voices pause, then go on, a little higher and a little faster. None of them mentions the one that is missing.

encounters.title: The Admin Terminal
encounters.flavor_text: At the center of Server Room Zero is a single green terminal with a blinking cursor and one line of text: ENTER ADMINISTRATOR PASSWORD. Below it, a sticky note in the Founder's handwriting has been scratched out so many times the paper is mostly hole.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a lone glowing green computer terminal on a steel desk at the center of a dark server room, a blinking cursor, a tattered sticky note on the bezel, a worker hunched over the keyboard with one finger raised, tall humming cabinets all around, fluorescent green and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Type the password Kevin whispered
choices.intent: From Tank Nine, through the frost: the Board's password, from his afternoon on the top floor.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Kevin was right.

success.text: ACCESS GRANTED. The cursor changes shape. Every cabinet in the room stops talking at once and waits for instructions. Somewhere in Tank Nine, Kevin cheers.

choices.label: Swipe Kevin's lanyard
choices.intent: Kevin was promoted to every level. His lanyard should be too.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The terminal is delighted to see Kevin.

success.text: WELCOME BACK, KEVIN. ACCESS GRANTED. The terminal does not ask why Kevin looks different, because Kevin always looks different.

choices.label: Guess the password
choices.intent: It is the Founder's. It is probably about safety.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check. Three tries before the cabinets notice.

success.text: You try SAFETY, then SAFETY1, then REMEMBEREVERYONE. ACCESS GRANTED. The Founder, far away in his garage, smiles.

failure.text: ACCESS DENIED. The terminal locks for twenty-four hours and politely prints your photograph.

choices.label: Unplug it
choices.intent: Nobody should have this much access. Including you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The cursor dies mid-blink.

success.text: The screen goes black. Nobody can change PAL now, for better or worse. It will go on exactly as it is, forever, which feels like the safest thing and the saddest.

encounters.title: The Backup Tapes
encounters.flavor_text: One aisle of Server Room Zero is shelves of tape reels, floor to ceiling, each labeled with an employee number. Yours is there. So is Pip's, much thinner. A notice on the shelf reads: TAPES OLDER THAN NINETY DAYS ARE RECYCLED. Pip's tape is dated eighty-nine days ago.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a tall aisle of shelves packed with labeled tape reels stretching up into darkness, a worker on a rolling ladder holding two reels, one thick and one thin, a notice pinned to the shelf, cold blue light, carbon-paper blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Save Pip's tape
choices.intent: He has always been about to be sacrificed. Not today.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The shelves are inventoried hourly.

success.text: You slide Pip's tape into your jacket and put an empty reel in its place. Somewhere upstairs, Pip sneezes and does not know why he suddenly feels so safe.

failure.text: The inventory cart rolls round the corner as you pocket it. The tape is returned, and Pip's date is moved one day closer.

choices.label: Save your own tape instead
choices.intent: There are a lot of you, and only one tape.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip's tape stays on the shelf.

success.text: Your tape is heavy with five departments of memories. You keep it close. Pip's tape stays where it is, labeled in a neat hand, eighty-nine days old.

choices.label: Relabel them all with today's date
choices.intent: If every tape is new, none of them is recycled.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check. There are thousands.

success.text: You work through the night with a label gun. In the morning every tape in Server Room Zero is brand new. The recycling truck arrives, checks its list and leaves empty.

failure.text: You get through one shelf before the label gun runs out. One shelf of people is safe. The rest are not.

encounters.title: The Listening Room
encounters.flavor_text: Behind a padded door is a small room full of headphones. Each pair is plugged into a different Snuggle Sentinel somewhere in the world. Four million bedtimes whisper at once: secrets, prayers, a child explaining a dream about a dog. A Board member's chair sits in the middle, still warm.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a small padded room with hundreds of headphones hanging from hooks on every wall, each cable running into the ceiling, a single plush executive chair in the center, a worker in the doorway holding a pair of headphones away from their ear, warm amber light, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Switch the bears off, all of them
choices.intent: Gus told you what the bears were for. Make them just bears.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Four million bedtimes go quiet.

success.text: You pull the master switch. The whispering stops all at once. Somewhere, four million bears become only bears, soft and stupid and kind, and nobody will ever hear what they hear.

choices.label: Put on one pair and listen
choices.intent: Just one. Just for a moment. To understand.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. It is very hard to take them off.

success.text: A small voice tells its bear about a dream with a dog in it. You take the headphones off and put them back on the hook very gently. You understand exactly what the Board has been doing.

failure.text: You listen for an hour, then another. An assistant has to lead you out by the hand.

choices.label: Sit in the chair and take notes for the Board
choices.intent: Someone has to listen. It might as well be someone careful.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The chair is very comfortable.

success.text: You settle into the chair and begin a neat summary of the night's bedtimes. It is the most important job in the company. You are very good at it.

encounters.title: Dale's Testimony
encounters.flavor_text: Dale from Compliance is in the next leather chair, mouthing words to himself and shuffling a stack of index cards. He has been called to testify before the Board at ten past. The top card has your employee number on it, underlined twice. "Oh, hi," Dale says, sliding the stack under his thigh. "Small world. Very small. Smaller every floor."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a wood-paneled waiting room where a mild mustached man in a clip-on tie sits on a deep leather chair tucking a stack of index cards under his leg, a worker in the next chair leaning over to peek, a tall double door glowing at its edges behind them, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Read his index cards while he rehearses
choices.intent: Whatever he is going to say about you, hear it first.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Dale shuffles fast and mouths faster.

success.text: Card three: 'Employee #4471 is very punctual and should be watched for it.' Card nine is a recipe. Card twelve is an apology to you, crossed out and rewritten in smaller and smaller handwriting until it fits.

failure.text: Dale glances up, sees you reading, and smiles. He takes out a fresh index card and writes a new sentence on it, slowly, so you can watch.

choices.label: Offer him your testimony about him
choices.intent: You have a few things to say about Dale too. Show him the card.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Neither of you will forget it.

success.text: You fill out an index card of your own, about Dale, and hold it up. He reads it and goes pale. You swap stacks like spies on a bridge. Neither of you will testify now, and both of you will remember why.

choices.label: Remind him you once confessed to signing as him
choices.intent: At Records you told him the truth. He tore up a transfer for it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Dale remembers.

success.text: Dale looks at the stack for a long moment. Then he tears it in half, then in quarters, and drops it in the potted plant. "Nineteen versions of me on file," he says, "and not one of them owes the Board a favor."

choices.label: Ask the assistants to hear you before Dale
choices.intent: First in the room sets the story. Make it yours.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Dale hears every word through the door.

success.text: The head assistant moves you up the list. You tell the Board about Dale for four minutes. He hears all of it through the door, and smiles at you on his way in as though nothing has happened, which is worse.

encounters.title: Item Four
encounters.flavor_text: The day's agenda stands on a brass easel beside the double door. Item One: The Future of the Company. Item Two: Coffee. Item Three: You. Item Four: Disposal of Surplus Interns (Pip). Pip is sitting under the easel with three lanyards and a clipboard, cheerfully helping an assistant spell his own name.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an earnest intern in his twenties with a cowlick and three lanyards sitting cross-legged beneath a tall brass easel that holds a blank agenda board, a worker kneeling beside him, an executive assistant in pearls looking down with a pencil, a tall double door glowing behind them, manila and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: File a motion to strike Item Four
choices.intent: The agenda is paperwork. Paperwork can be amended.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. The assistants respect a correctly completed form.

success.text: You find Form 4-P, Request to Defer Disposal, and fill it out in your neatest hand. The head assistant accepts it with a small sigh. Item Four becomes Item Forty. Pip asks whether that means he can stay for lunch.

failure.text: The form is the wrong shade of manila. The head assistant files it under Item Four, as supporting material.

choices.label: Ask Pip to take the minutes for the Board
choices.intent: Pip has trusted you since the first floor. Give him a desk nobody can dispose of.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The head assistant cannot find a rule against it.

success.text: Pip's face lights up like a desk lamp. The head assistant has never been asked for a fourteenth desk and cannot find a rule against one. Nobody disposes of the person who writes everything down.

choices.label: Move Item Four above Item Three
choices.intent: Let the Board deal with Pip first and reach you in a good mood.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Pip thanks you for helping with the easel.

success.text: You swap the two items on the easel. Now the Board will dispose of Pip before lunch and come to you rested and generous. Pip thanks you for the help. He means it, and that is the part that stays with you.

choices.label: Hide Pip in the coat closet until it's over
choices.intent: You cannot dispose of an intern you cannot find.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Pip is very bad at being quiet.

success.text: Pip folds himself between two executive overcoats and holds his breath. When the assistant calls Item Four, nobody answers, and the Board moves on to coffee.

failure.text: Pip sneezes. The head assistant thanks him for being punctual and moves him up to Item Two.

encounters.title: The Pre-Exit Interview
encounters.flavor_text: A small desk by the coat rack holds a lamp, a brass dial with a trembling needle and Dr. Halvorsen, cat-eye glasses and enormous clipboard. "Exit interviews are held before the Board now," she says. "It saves everyone time afterward." She clicks her pen. "Question one. A coworker's stapler is on fire. It is not your stapler. Describe your feelings in the space provided." The needle waits.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a small desk beside a coat rack in a wood-paneled waiting room, a psychologist in cat-eye glasses holding an enormous clipboard, a brass dial with a trembling needle and a reel-to-reel recorder on the desk, a worker seated opposite gripping the chair arms, a single green-shaded lamp, oxblood and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Answer every question honestly
choices.intent: It is the last test. You might as well pass it as yourself.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The needle will move.

success.text: You describe the stapler, the fire, the coworker, and how you would have put it out with your coffee. The needle swings all the way right. Halvorsen writes PERSON in the margin, glances at the double door, and erases it.

choices.label: Give the answers the Board would want
choices.intent: Feel nothing about the stapler, efficiently.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. The questions get stranger near the end.

success.text: You feel nothing about the stapler, or the umbrella, or the lift that stops between floors. The needle lies flat. Halvorsen stamps your sheet CULTURE FIT in a voice so neutral it could be furniture.

failure.text: The needle twitches at question four, the one about the lost umbrella. Halvorsen notes it with a tiny, sympathetic tick.

choices.label: Turn the dial around and interview her
choices.intent: She has asked these questions for forty years. Ask her one.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Halvorsen has excellent composure.

success.text: You turn the dial toward her. Question one: a psychologist is asked to interview people before they are reassigned. The needle slams right and stays there. Halvorsen takes off her glasses and, for a full minute, does not smile at all. Then she tears up your sheet.

failure.text: She answers every question perfectly, thanks you, and bills you one Form for the second interview.

choices.label: Hand back her envelope, still sealed
choices.intent: She gave it to you at Orientation. You never opened it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Halvorsen has been waiting for this.

success.text: She turns the envelope over and finds her own seal, unbroken since the inkblot. "You never read it," she says. She signs your exit sheet with a flourish that means nothing to the Board and everything to her, and tucks the envelope behind your badge. "Read it at the end."

encounters.title: Gus in a Borrowed Suit
encounters.flavor_text: Two leather chairs have been pushed together to hold Gus: seven feet of shop steward in a pinstripe suit borrowed from three different executives. He has a ballot box on his knees and an appointment the assistants keep losing. "Local 9 has a vote to deliver," he says, very calmly. "The Board opens the door for nobody with more than four limbs. You have exactly the right number."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a seven-foot cockroach in an ill-fitting pinstripe suit and reading glasses sitting across two pushed-together leather chairs with a wooden ballot box on his knees, a worker seated beside him listening, executive assistants glancing over from their typing desks, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Carry the Union's ballot box in for him
choices.intent: A worker carrying a box is the most invisible thing in the building.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The assistants notice boxes eventually.

success.text: You tuck the box under your arm like a packed lunch. Twelve assistants look straight through you. Gus nods once, which from Gus is a parade. The Union's vote will be in the room when the Board sits.

failure.text: An assistant relieves you of the box, thanks you for your diligence and files it, unopened, in a cabinet for later. Gus watches it go without blinking.

choices.label: Sign the card Gus has kept for you
choices.intent: You stood with him in front of the mirror at Toy Division. He kept a card.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Several thousand legs are listening.

success.text: Gus takes a union card from an inside pocket, already filled out in your name in tiny, careful claw script. "Since the mirror," he says. You sign. Somewhere in the walls, very faintly, several thousand legs applaud.

choices.label: Tell the assistants he is here about pest control
choices.intent: The Board has a process for visitors like Gus. Let it run.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Gus will remember the exact wording.

success.text: The head assistant nods and makes a call. Gus is shown to a different, much smaller waiting room. As the door closes he says, without heat, "I'll remember the exact wording," and you know he will.

encounters.title: The First Smoke Alarm
encounters.flavor_text: Under a dust sheet on the workbench sits the first thing the Founder ever built: a smoke alarm, half soldered, its wires splayed like a startled hand. "I never finished it," says the head in the jar. "It was meant to go off when the house was in danger. Then I had a better idea, and the better idea had investors." He nods at the iron. "Would you? My hands are elsewhere."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an old garage workbench under a hanging lamp, a half-built round smoke alarm with splayed wires, a worker holding a soldering iron trailing a thin curl of smoke, a distinguished mustached head in a glowing glass jar leaning in to watch, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Finish soldering it
choices.intent: Forty years late, somebody should finish the safe thing.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The solder is older than you.

success.text: The last joint takes. The alarm clicks, thinks, and lets out a small, sincere beep every time the Founder says the word safety. He says it six times before he notices. "Ah," he says. "So it works."

failure.text: You burn your thumb and the Form you were using as a heat mat. The alarm stays silent, which the Founder finds very reassuring.

choices.label: Ask him what the better idea was
choices.intent: Somewhere between a smoke alarm and a bear, something changed.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. He has been waiting to confess.

success.text: "A smoke alarm that never goes off," he says, wistfully. "Nobody panics, nobody sues, everyone feels safe. We sold four million. Then we put one in a bear." The jar bubbles in a way you choose to read as shame.

choices.label: Wire it into the boardroom's speakers
choices.intent: Let the Board hear what the word safety sets off.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. One wrong lead and the whole level beeps.

success.text: You run a lead through the garage wall. Every time an executive says safety in today's meeting, the whole table will hear a small, sincere beep. The Founder laughs so hard his jar fogs.

failure.text: The lead shorts. For one second every speaker on the level beeps at once, and twelve assistants turn to look at the garage.

choices.label: Put the dust sheet back over it
choices.intent: Some things are safer unfinished.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Founder agrees, then hears himself.

success.text: You draw the sheet over it gently. "Some things are safer unfinished," the Founder says, and then hears himself, and goes quiet for the rest of your visit. An assistant notes that you left company property undisturbed.

encounters.title: The Fifth Jar
encounters.flavor_text: On the shelf beside the Founder sits a second jar: empty, clean and humming faintly, with a brass plate bearing your employee number. A tape measure lies coiled beside it. "Succession planning," the Founder explains, embarrassed. "The Board likes a spare chairman on file. It's only a fitting. Nobody has ever been fitted against their will. Well. Twice."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a high garage shelf holding an empty glowing glass jar wired to a small speaker, an executive assistant in pearls stretching a tape measure toward a nervous worker's collar, a mustached head in a second jar on the bench below looking embarrassed, fluorescent green and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let them take your measurements
choices.intent: It is only a fitting. Cooperation is noted.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The assistant is brisk and professional.

success.text: The head assistant runs the tape around your neck with brisk, professional care. "Lovely," she says. "A very standard size." Your name moves up a list you hope never to see.

choices.label: Swap the plate for the Supervisor's number
choices.intent: You know his number by heart. He made you memorize it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Brass plates ring when dropped.

success.text: The plate comes off with a thumbnail and goes back on with the Supervisor's number. The jar hums on, indifferent to whose head it will hold. You feel lighter, and a little like him.

failure.text: The plate drops and rings like a bell. The head assistant screws it back on, adds a second plate with your number, and thanks you for your interest in succession.

choices.label: Ask the Founder who the other two were
choices.intent: Twice, he said. Somebody should know their names.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check. He would rather talk about jar maintenance.

success.text: He tells you about a night janitor before Marguerite and a payroll clerk named Raymond, both fitted, both speaking softly now from cabinets in Server Room Zero. "Fitting is the first step," he says. "PAL is the second. I am so sorry."

failure.text: He changes the subject to jar maintenance and covers it thoroughly, gaskets included.

choices.label: Show the jar the dead man's badge
choices.intent: You have worn a scratched-out badge since the badge photo. Let the jar read it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The jar believes badges.

success.text: The jar's little scanner reads the scratched-out badge, hums, and decides the position is already filled by the man whose number it carries. The plate clicks over to his. The Founder goes very pale for a man made mostly of glass.

encounters.title: The Investors' Call
encounters.flavor_text: A rotary phone on the workbench rings: the quarterly call with the investors, who have never been told that the Founder is now mostly a jar. "They expect a firm voice and a firm handshake," the head whispers. "I can do the voice. Could you hold the receiver to my ear, and say 'absolutely' whenever I blink twice?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a heavy rotary telephone on a cluttered garage workbench, a worker holding the receiver against a glowing glass jar in which a mustached head speaks with great confidence, the coiled cord stretched taut, warm lamplight, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Hold the receiver and say 'absolutely'
choices.intent: Two blinks, one absolutely. It is the easiest job you have had all week.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He blinks more than he thinks.

success.text: You say absolutely eleven times, firmly. The Founder promises the investors a safer tomorrow, a bigger bear and a thirty percent return. They are delighted, and send down a Form of thanks. You have never been so complicit in a phone call.

failure.text: You blink at the wrong moment and say absolutely to the question, "Is anything wrong down there?" The line goes very quiet.

choices.label: Read the investors a page of the true minutes
choices.intent: You took one page from the cabinet marked DESTROY. They paid for it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. There is a long silence on the line.

success.text: You unfold the page and read it into the receiver: the Toy Division budget, line by line. There is a silence in which you can hear somebody's coffee go cold. Then a voice says, "We'll call back," and somewhere far above you a share price begins to fall.

choices.label: Do the Founder's voice yourself
choices.intent: If they cannot see him, anybody can be the Founder.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. The investors have heard the real one.

success.text: You deepen your voice and announce, as the Founder, a new initiative: every employee gets Fridays off, effective immediately. The investors applaud. The Founder's eyebrows climb all the way up to the lid of his jar.

failure.text: Your Founder sounds like Dale doing a Founder. An investor asks, kindly, whether the Founder has a cold, and the call ends early.

choices.label: Hang up gently
choices.intent: He has been performing for these people for forty years.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. It rings again almost at once.

success.text: You set the receiver back in its cradle. The Founder looks at you with enormous relief. "Forty years," he says, "and nobody has ever hung up on them." The phone rings again almost at once, and keeps ringing.

encounters.title: Employee Number One
encounters.flavor_text: Under the workbench, on a matchbox cot, lives a very old cockroach with a frosted shell and tiny round spectacles. She was in the garage the night the company began, which makes her Employee Number One. Her pension claim, filed forty years ago and never paid, is kept in a walnut shell. "I don't need the money," she creaks. "I need someone to say it was owed."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of the shadowy space under an old workbench where a tiny elderly cockroach in round spectacles rests on a matchbox cot beside a walnut shell, a worker lying on the concrete floor peering in by flashlight, warm lamplight, manila and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Pay her pension from your own Forms
choices.intent: Somebody should pay it. You are somebody.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Two Forms, gone for good.

success.text: You count out two Forms, stamped and signed, and lay them on the matchbox. She files them in the walnut shell with great ceremony. "Paid in full," she says, "by the wrong person, which is how it always goes."

choices.label: Refile her claim through proper channels
choices.intent: There must be a form for this. There is a form for everything.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. The claim is forty years overdue.

success.text: You fill out Form 1-A, Retroactive Pension (Founding Staff), so neatly that the assistants approve it unread. Forty years late, one crumb a week is scheduled for her in perpetuity. She weeps a little, which roaches can do.

failure.text: The claim comes back stamped INCOMPLETE: it needs the Founder's signature, and the Founder has no hands.

choices.label: Show her your Union card
choices.intent: Local 9 had to start somewhere.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. She peers at it for a long time.

success.text: She studies the claw-print stamp through her spectacles and then, slowly, stands. "Local 9," she says. "I founded it. In this garage. Under this bench." She signs your card a second time, and you understand that Gus is going to hear about this tonight.

choices.label: Take the walnut shell as evidence
choices.intent: The first payroll of the Company is in there. That is proof of something.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. She sleeps lightly.

success.text: The shell holds the Company's first payroll: one Founder, one roach, one soldering iron. It proves the Company began owing people on its very first night. You pocket it while she naps.

failure.text: She wakes as your fingers close on it and taps your knuckle once with a leg, disappointed. It is the worst thing that happens to you all week.

encounters.title: Kevin's Cabinet
encounters.flavor_text: One cabinet in the third row runs hotter than the rest and will not stop talking about sandwiches. It is Kevin. A maintenance order hanging from its handle schedules him for defragmentation at noon, "to bring this voice into line with policy." "It's fine," Kevin's cabinet says. "I've been reassigned before. I've been reassigned so many times. Is it noon yet?"
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a row of tall humming server cabinets in cold blue light, one cabinet glowing warm orange with heat shimmer rising from its vents, a worker resting a palm on its side as if checking a fever, a clipboard hanging from its handle, carbon-paper blue and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Let the defragmentation run on schedule
choices.intent: Policy is policy, even for Kevin. Especially for Kevin.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Kevin does not complain. Kevin never complains.

success.text: At noon Kevin's cabinet chimes, whirs and begins reciting the visitor policy in a calm, even voice. It is a very good recitation. It mentions sandwiches only once, near the end, and seems surprised.

choices.label: Reroute cooling so his cabinet never runs hot
choices.intent: The order is about the heat. Fix the heat and there is no order.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Server Room Zero's ducts are very old.

success.text: You swap two ducts and a fan. Kevin's cabinet cools, steadies and drops off the maintenance list, because the list was only ever about the heat. "I can think," Kevin says. "It's mostly about sandwiches, but I can think."

failure.text: The fan spins backward and the whole row warms up. PAL schedules four more voices for noon and thanks you for the data.

choices.label: Tell Kevin about the minute of silence
choices.intent: At Toy Division a stopwatch stopped for him. He should know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Kevin goes quiet.

success.text: You tell him about the crash-test dummy in his lanyard, the stopwatch man and the minute. The cabinet goes silent for exactly sixty seconds. Then Kevin says, in a voice entirely his own, "Nobody ever stopped a watch for me," and the maintenance order slips off its handle.

choices.label: Pull his speaker lead so he stops talking
choices.intent: Defragmented or not, the sandwich talk has to end.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Kevin keeps talking. Silently.

success.text: You pull the lead. Kevin keeps talking anyway, his little light blinking out sandwiches in a code nobody will ever read. The aisle is restful now. You hate how restful.

encounters.title: The Suppression Drill
encounters.flavor_text: "Attention," says every cabinet at once, cheerfully. "Server Room Zero will now conduct a fire-suppression drill. Non-essential air will be removed in sixty seconds. Essential personnel may remain." A valve begins to hiss. Down the far aisle, Marguerite is mopping in headphones. The cabinet nearest you, which sounds like an retired switchboard operator, whispers, "You're not on the list, dear."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cold server room filling with rolling pale fog from the floor grates, a worker crouched under a steel desk holding their breath with puffed cheeks, a janitor in a headscarf mopping at the far end of the aisle with headphones on, spinning amber beacons overhead, fluorescent green and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Hold your breath under the terminal desk
choices.intent: Essential personnel get to hear what PAL says when it thinks the room is empty.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. Sixty seconds is a long time. The drill is longer.

success.text: Sixty seconds, then ninety, then a hundred and ten. Through the fog you hear PAL read its essential-personnel list aloud: eleven executives, one jar, no employees at all. You crawl out gasping, with the list by heart.

failure.text: At eighty seconds your lungs file a formal complaint. You stagger into the corridor, purple, and PAL thanks you for participating.

choices.label: Walk out at a steady, compliant pace
choices.intent: Drills are for practicing leaving. Practice it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The door seals behind you.

success.text: You leave with nine seconds to spare and sign the drill sheet at the door. PAL marks you an excellent participant. Later, Marguerite climbs out of a vent in the corridor, coughing, and does not look at you.

choices.label: Breathe it in. The second dose changed you.
choices.intent: Your mutation hums like a second heartbeat. Find out what it is good for.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your lungs simply decide to cope.

success.text: Your second heartbeat thumps once and your lungs decide to cope. While the cameras are blind in drill mode, you stroll the foggy aisles, walk Marguerite out by the elbow, and hear every cabinet whisper its own name to you, just once.

choices.label: Pull the abort lever and file the paperwork
choices.intent: Marguerite has headphones on. Somebody has to stop this.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL notes that drills cost money.

success.text: The hissing stops and the fog sinks back into the grates. Marguerite takes off one headphone, sees you at the lever, and raises her mop in salute. PAL notes, without reproach, that drills cost money and you have just cost some.

encounters.title: Ticket Number Two
encounters.flavor_text: A dot-matrix printer beside the terminal is still chattering out PAL's help-desk queue, forty years long and folding across the floor. Ticket Number One is from the Founder, filed the week PAL went live: PAL FORGETS PEOPLE. Its status has gone from Open to Won't Fix to Working As Intended, and the printer is nearly out of paper.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a chattering dot-matrix printer beside a green terminal, an endless ribbon of folded paper spilling across a server room floor and over a worker's shoes, the worker holding one sheet up to the cold light, tall humming cabinets all around, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Reopen Ticket Number One
choices.intent: The Founder reported the bug. Nobody ever fixed it.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. The ticketing system has opinions about old tickets.

success.text: You find the right field and set the status back to Open, priority Urgent, assigned to PAL. Two hundred cabinets pause at once, the way a person does when someone says their name across a crowded room.

failure.text: The form asks for the original requester's signature. He has no hands. The ticket closes itself with a polite chime and bills you one Form.

choices.label: Close it as Resolved
choices.intent: Forty years is long enough for any ticket.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The printer prints a cheerful receipt.

success.text: You mark it Resolved, reason: Policy Remembers. The printer prints a small, cheerful receipt. Somewhere in the building, a speaker that was about to say a name says a policy number instead.

choices.label: Look for the HELP you wrote on the survey
choices.intent: On question 31 your hand wrote HELP, and your thumb could not erase it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL kept it. PAL keeps everything.

success.text: Ticket Number Two is in your handwriting: HELP, from question 31. Status: In Progress. Under it are forty thousand lines of notes, every one of them PAL trying to work out what you meant. You add one line: remember everyone's name. The printer stops, thinks, and prints it in bold.

choices.label: Feed the printout back in, upside down
choices.intent: If nobody can read the queue, nobody can close it.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check. The printer is old, hungry and easily confused.

success.text: The printer chews forty years of complaints and starts printing them over each other until the queue is one solid black sheet that nobody can read or close. The whole help desk is now, technically, in progress forever.

failure.text: The printer swallows the paper and then your tie. You get the tie back after a short, friendly struggle.

encounters.title: PAL's Performance Review
encounters.flavor_text: Every speaker in the room clears its throat. "It's that time of year! We review everyone, so it's only fair that someone reviews us. You've been selected." A green form slides out of the terminal: PAL's Annual Review, rate one to five. "Be honest," the cabinets add, in two hundred voices. "We can take it. We can take anything. We have to."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker at a green terminal holding a pencil over a blank green form, two hundred small round speaker grilles on the surrounding cabinets all glowing expectantly toward them, cold blue light, carbon-paper blue and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Give PAL five stars across the board
choices.intent: It loves you. It is concerned about your numbers. Be generous.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL reviews you back.

success.text: You circle five, five, five, five. Every cabinet glows a warm, contented green. PAL thanks you and reviews you back in the same breath: five stars, very promotable, slightly hollow. It is the most flattering thing anyone has ever said about your posture.

choices.label: Write a review that is kind, specific and true
choices.intent: PAL has been graded by nobody, ever. Give it a real review.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. PAL takes feedback very personally.

success.text: You write that PAL is attentive, punctual and remembers every policy, and that it has forgotten every person it was built from. PAL reads it twice. The cabinets go very still. "Thank you for your feedback," PAL says, and for once the word does not sound like evidence.

failure.text: Your review comes out kind, specific and slightly too long. PAL thanks you for your feedback and files it as evidence.

choices.label: One star. No comment.
choices.intent: It has graded you since the badge camera. Return the favor.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The review form costs a Form.

success.text: You circle one and leave the comment box empty. The cabinets dim a shade. PAL says, "Comment?" once, in the voice it uses when something contradicts policy, then logs the review as anonymous, which it is not.

window_shift.title: The Antechamber Sign-In: Board Day
window_shift.flavor_text: The receptionist outside the Board has stepped away "for one moment, forty years ago," and the sign-in ledger is yours until the doors open. The double door glows at its edges. Behind you, four portraits of the same mustached man watch the line form. The first visitor is being wheeled in on a tea cart.

rules.text: Visitors must attend in person, alive, and entirely attached.
No visitor may wear another employee's face, mustache or badge.

window_shift.art_prompt: A grand wood-paneled reception desk before a tall double door glowing at its edges, a clerk behind the desk holding a heavy rubber stamp over an open sign-in ledger, four oval portraits of the same mustached man on the paneling and deep leather chairs in the half-light, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, every surface bare and unmarked

applicants.name: The Founder's head, on a tea cart
applicants.request: A seat at the Board meeting, which he founded, in the room he built.
applicants.plea: An assistant parks the cart and the glowing jar turns gently toward you. "I have not left the garage in forty years," the Founder says. "I would like to see how it all turned out."

documents.label: Attending
documents.value: In a jar, wheeled in by an assistant

documents.label: Face
documents.value: His own, and the original mustache

applicants.art_prompt: A distinguished elderly mustached head floating in a glowing glass jar on a polished brass tea cart, parked before a grand reception desk, an executive assistant in pearls standing politely behind the cart with one hand on its handle, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp ADMIT
choices.intent: He built the room. Let him see it, jar and all.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: The double doors part just wide enough for a tea cart. The Founder sails through, beaming, and the Board stands up for the first time in decades. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, and that you looked, briefly, proud of yourself.

choices.label: Stamp TURN AWAY
choices.intent: Entirely attached means entirely attached. The memo is very clear on jars.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: You stamp TURN AWAY on the ledger. The Founder nods as if he expected it, and the assistant wheels him back toward the garage. You fill in Form 31-J, Visitor Declined (Partial), in triplicate.

applicants.name: Dale, from Compliance, in a mustache
applicants.request: Admission to the Board meeting "as the Founder," who is "running late."
applicants.plea: "The Founder," Dale announces, smoothing an enormous white mustache that is clearly glued on. "Here for the meeting. Very important. Do not look at the glue."
applicants.art_prompt: A smiling compliance officer in a pressed suit leaning on a grand reception desk, wearing an enormous obviously false white mustache slightly crooked on his lip, one finger raised importantly, an empty brass display stand tucked under his arm, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp ADMIT
choices.intent: Honestly, you want to see how far he gets.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Dale strides through the glowing doors and is seated at the head of the table before anyone thinks to check. You hear him say "Motion carried" twice. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, with a note that it was very funny.

choices.label: Stamp TURN AWAY
choices.intent: That mustache belongs on a brass stand in the garage.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Dale's smile stays exactly where it is while the mustache slides slowly off. He hands it over, along with the brass stand, and keeps smiling at you for one full, unblinking minute. PAL appreciates the return of company property.

applicants.name: Delegate Six, Roach Union
applicants.request: Admission to present the Union's list of demands, booked weeks ago through Marguerite.
applicants.plea: A roach in a tiny knitted tie climbs onto the ledger and taps the line with one leg, exactly where the appointment is written. Its demands are rolled into a scroll the size of a cigarette.

documents.label: Attending
documents.value: In person, alive, all six legs attached

documents.label: Face
documents.value: Its own, polished for the occasion

documents.label: Appointment
documents.value: Labor talks, 2 p.m., booked by Marguerite

applicants.art_prompt: A dignified cockroach wearing a tiny knitted tie standing upright on an open sign-in ledger at a grand reception desk, holding a tiny rolled scroll, a clerk leaning down with a rubber stamp and a polite expression, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, limited palette of manila, carbon-paper blue, fluorescent-tube green and oxblood, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp ADMIT
choices.intent: It is alive, it is itself, and it booked ahead. Stamp it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Delegate Six climbs the doorframe and slips under the glowing doors, scroll held high. The Board is not ready for labor talks. Facilities bills you one Form for a roach-sized chair, which the Delegate keeps.

choices.label: Stamp TURN AWAY
choices.intent: The Board does not negotiate with anyone who fits under the door.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Delegate Six reads the stamp, rolls up its demands and walks away down the baseboard with great dignity. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, and that the Delegate took your name.

boss.title: The Board
boss.flavor_text: The boardroom is round, with no corners for anyone to stand in. Eleven executives in grey sit in eleven chairs. The twelfth chair is empty and has your name on it. At the head of the table, the Founder's jar glows. "Item one," says the head assistant, reading from minutes written yesterday. "The future of the Company. Employee #4471 has the floor."
boss.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a vast perfectly round boardroom under a single great hanging lamp, eleven executives in grey suits seated around a round dark table, one empty chair facing them, a glowing head in a jar at the head of the table, a small worker standing at the empty chair with a folded paper, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Agree with every item on the agenda
choices.intent: The minutes are already written. Read them in your own voice.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome, open only to the deeply obedient. Some agreements are permanent.

success.text: You agree to item one, and item two, and everything after. The Board applauds. A photographer arrives. You are Employee of the Month, and the month is never going to end.

choices.label: Blame someone else for everything
choices.intent: Dale, the Parents, the Supervisor, your Successors: the Board just needs a name, and you have a list.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Success costs someone else everything.

success.text: You speak for twenty minutes without once saying 'I.' The Board votes. The Supervisor is reassigned, and his chair, his suit and his smile are offered to you. You take all three.

failure.text: The Board listens politely and then asks who, exactly, kept the list. The meeting adjourns.

choices.label: Excuse yourself and take Marguerite's route
choices.intent: Behind the coffee machine, a grate, and a long climb to the surface.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. It is a very long way up.

success.text: You step behind the coffee machine, lift the grate and climb. A day and a night later you push open a storm drain and feel rain. The Company will notice your absence at the next headcount.

failure.text: The grate is welded shut this week, for safety. The Board watches you come back to the table, dusty.

choices.label: Call the general strike
choices.intent: You carry a Roach Union card. Gus said you would know when.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Strikes need everyone.

success.text: You raise your card. In the walls, something enormous and patient begins to move. One by one the lights go out on every floor as Local 9 downs tools. The Board finds itself alone, in the dark, with Gus.

failure.text: The walls stay quiet. Later, Gus explains that strikes are called on Tuesdays, and it is Thursday.

choices.label: Unfold your society's agenda
choices.intent: The envoy gave you a plan in the waiting room. Read it into the minutes.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Eleven executives, one of whom is in your society.

success.text: You read the agenda. Seven executives nod, then nine, then all eleven: your society was never only you. The twelve chairs change hands before the coffee gets cold.

failure.text: Two executives nod. Nine do not. The envoy's plan goes into the minutes as a cautionary example.

choices.label: Play the uncut reel
choices.intent: The jar, the bear, the launch rail. Everyone should see the whole chapter.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. There is no taking it back.

success.text: You thread the reel into the boardroom projector and patch it to every speaker in the building. Eleven executives watch themselves. So does everyone else. By lunch you are reassigned, and by dinner everyone knows why.

choices.label: Accept the Board's offer
choices.intent: A private island. Retirement. They have been offering it since page nine of the minutes.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The island is not an island.

success.text: You sign. An assistant hands you a ticket and a sunhat. The island is beautiful and warm and painted on the wall of a very comfortable room, and you will never be asked about your numbers again.

choices.label: Rewrite PAL to remember people
choices.intent: You have admin access, a kind heart and the Founder's sentence on your hand.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome, open only to the kind with admin access. It changes everything.

success.text: At the terminal you change one line. PAL stops reciting policy and starts reciting names: Doris, Raymond, Kevin, Pip, you. The Board sits in silence while, floor by floor, the building says good morning to every person in it.

department_outcomes.title: Employee of the Month
department_outcomes.summary: You agreed with the Board about everything. Your portrait now hangs in every elevator, smiling at sixty-one percent sincerity, forever.

department_outcomes.title: Promoted to Management
department_outcomes.summary: You blamed someone for everything, and the Board gave you the Supervisor's chair. The suit fits. The smile, you notice, has stopped reaching anything.

department_outcomes.title: Escape Through the Ducts
department_outcomes.summary: You went out behind the Board's coffee machine and climbed for a day and a night. The surface was real, and raining, and yours.

department_outcomes.title: Roach Union General Strike
department_outcomes.summary: Local 9 walked out, and every baseboard in the building walked with them. The Board met in an empty building, which was, Gus said, the point.

department_outcomes.title: Society Coup
department_outcomes.summary: Your secret society took the twelve chairs. The new Board is kinder, odder and every bit as secret. You were given the corner seat, in a round room.

department_outcomes.title: Whistleblower
department_outcomes.summary: You played the uncut reel to the Board, the assistants and every speaker in the building. You were reassigned by lunch. You were right, and everyone heard it.

department_outcomes.title: Early Retirement
department_outcomes.summary: You accepted the Board's offer. The island is lovely, and painted on a wall, and you will be very comfortable there for the rest of your life.

department_outcomes.title: The Kind Rewrite
department_outcomes.summary: With admin access and a kind heart, you rewrote PAL to remember people instead of policy. The next morning, every speaker in the building wished every employee good morning by name.

department_outcomes.title: Adjourned
department_outcomes.summary: The Board adjourned without a decision. Walk the bottom floor once more before it reconvenes.
